name: Shel Talmy
hook: An American who talked his way into a London studio and ended up producing the Kinks and the Who within a year of each other.
blurb: Talmy was a Chicago-born producer who moved to London in the early 1960s. According to the widely repeated story, he got his first job partly by playing test pressings and letting people assume he had produced them himself. He went on to produce the Kinks' 'You Really Got Me' (1964) and the Who's 'I Can't Explain' (1965), giving both bands a harder, more compressed guitar sound than most British records of the time. He is the clearest case on this map of one producer carrying a sound between two otherwise unconnected bands. His contracts mattered as much as his ear: the Who's early records came out on Decca's UK Brunswick label because that was Talmy's arrangement, and when the band split from him in 1966 they left that label in the same move. He died in Los Angeles on 13 November 2024, aged 87.

signatureTracks.whyThisOne: The slashed-speaker-cone riff, recorded and mixed by Talmy into the hardest guitar sound on British radio that year.
